note: The source commit b903902 fixes the four write-path rounds and is the commit the pinned artifact was built from. b903902..facdcc2 is two commits: b3d6b4d re-pins the artifact, the checksum file and both host acceptance evidences after that acceptance, and facdcc2 is test-only. facdcc2 fixes the projection-free load round's too-deep fixture, which serialized an 8 000-level document with JSON.stringify; that call recursed once per level on Node 22/24 and overflowed the stack inside the fixture, so the case failed before it could compare the two trees. observations: The tag commit runs one commit ahead of the fixed source commit, and that commit only touches test/. commitContentDigest reads package.json#files from git objects, so the tagged tree digest is unchanged and the pin still holds; the release workflow enforced the same rule on the runner.

The candidate commit b3d6b4d had already been pushed with red unit-test jobs. Publishing it as tagged would have shipped a tag whose CI never passed, so the fix was made and CI re-run before the tag was created.

The vulnerable assumption was in the test fixture, not in lib/: JSON.stringify recursion depth is not a portable property, so the fixture must not depend on it. The deep document itself is still produced, and the port still refuses it with the same error on both engines.

`docs/evidence/dsh-<host>.json` remains the pin evidence referenced by release/manifest.json. The rc11-ci-* and rc11-postpublish-* files are additional records and are not referenced by pack:check or release-pin.test.mjs.
GitHub reports the rc.11 asset digest itself as sha256:c81b36b2…, so the published bytes are verifiable without trusting this repository.
remainingRisksAndUnverified: The released bytes are fixed by hand in release/ rather than rebuilt by CI (deliberate; pack:check, release:verify and release-pin.test.mjs make a silent divergence impossible, but they cannot prove the bytes came from the recorded source other than by content digest).
v0.2.0-rc.1's tag and its published asset disagree; that historical inconsistency is recorded in RELEASE.md section 6 and was not repaired (repairing it would move a tag or overwrite an asset).
The guard remains a heuristic policy check, not a shell/JavaScript sandbox; promotion runs cooperative host code behind a trusted approval.
The acceptance does not cover hand-disposing the bundle Fiber directly.
The promotion domain evaluator is advisory; promotionGates is the production authority.
lib/dockyard-domain/continuous and governance are unit-tested but not wired into the live loop.

Undocumented host surfaces are still used (ctx.events._hooks, ctx.reflect._getImpl()); runtime.internal-api degrades to `degraded` when they are missing, but every DSH upgrade must re-run the full acceptance.
Sustained external drift during a trial still refuses recovery.
event-bridge.key has no rotation or revocation flow.
No npm publish, no code signing / provenance (SLSA) and no SBOM.
The 0.2.1-alpha.1 npm dist-tag may move; the acceptance pins the exact version.
The file backend's failure memory is still last-writer-wins and save() does not fsync.

The shipped RELEASE.md still describes 0.2.0-rc.11 as a local candidate (it says no tag was created, no public entry point exists, and rc.10 is the last public release) because RELEASE.md is part of the package: editing it after the pin would move contentSha256, so the publication state is recorded in docs/evidence instead. The published Release notes are not stale - they name the real tag, its CI and the public download commands.

main is ahead of the tag by audit commits that only add files under docs/evidence. That is deliberate: the record for a release cannot live inside the pinned bytes, and `git log --name-only facdcc2..main` shows every such commit is docs-only. The shipped content digest of main still equals the pin.

The identity of the action that published the draft cannot be established from release metadata or workflow logs alone: the logs show the draft being created, its assets uploaded and verified, and no publish step, but publishing is a separate action outside CI.
